A common criticism of the unitiated to Bayesian inference is why we care about priors. I mean, to the early student of statistics, they just learned about _maximum likelihood estimation_ --- and wouldn't we always want the parameter that makes the data the _most_ likely? Why would we muddy that with our _subjective beliefs_; that surely can't be scientific! Over the course of this post, I'd like to argue why the prior is such a uesful concept both practically and scientifically and also show why often, as long as we begin somewhere reasonable, it often makes little difference in the end. But first: what even is a prior?
